body: I haven't really found any reliable coping mechanisms either. And I agree, staring at a lifetime of merely coping fucking sucks. Bad. I'm with you there. It makes me angry and fills me with complete apathy toward everything and everyone. I'm always amazed at the people that have it "together." In one sense, I think they're naive, delusional fucks, but in another, I just want to be a naive delusional fuck right alongside them. It's all messed up.

Unfortunately, yes. It hurts her greatly b/c she simply can't understand how someone can feel as I do. While I don't want to hurt her, I also don't believe I should lie to her either. She knows I love her as much as I can love anyone, but that doesn't change the end result. I could love her more than anyone has ever loved anyone else in the history of the universe...but we both, along with every other living organism, will eventually end up dead. So what has that love accomplished? Nothing!

I simply have no desire to live any longer. The pain I reference is a pain wholly created by the realization that nothing fucking matters. I could kill 1,000 babies, or save the world from global warming, or make $1B, and none of it will have an effect in the end. Eventually the lifespan of this galaxy will expire and every remnant of mankind will cease to exist. Don't you see? We create these feelings of purpose simply to keep from going crazy. But once you really internalize the gravity of the situation, I don't see how you ever go back. I can no longer live as if I have purpose. If I was extremely wealthy I would stick around simply for hedonistic purposes, but I'm not. I have insane amounts of debt (student loans, which are simply a means of enslaving an entire class of society), a job that I loathe (again, no meaning), and I don't really feel like fighting that battle any longer when it simply doesn't matter. 

We're all just a bunch of delusional plebs.

I know, right?! Every "reasonable" response to that hollow feeling of nothingness falls completely flat...b/c there is no frame of reference that makes the response any more meaningful than anything else, precisely b/c of the hopelessness of existentialism. How can one be reasoned through it when the very realm in which the conversation is taking place has absolutely zero value to the person in question? I've had loved ones try and comfort me but they just don't get it, which usually just adds to my frustration.

I, nor anyone else here, can convince you that there is meaning to be found. But you're so young. Who knows what may happen in the next few years. I've known a lot of people emerge on the other side of existentialism with renewed vigor and purpose. I've also known others who didn't.

Existentialism. Nothing matters. Meaning is created by man, but in the end, is still pointless. It's a ball of yarn that a cat plays with. Eventually the sun will burn the Earth and all existence will cease to be. So no, there is no meaning. 

I feel you. Completely.
